body:
_Migrated from issue #1386, filed 2026-08-05._

Follow-up from #1384 / #1385, which removed the severe instance of this class (the metadata.db lock poll loop, up to 120s of hub freeze).

Two smaller ones remain, both retrying a locked-SQLite read on a request path:

- `cps/web.py:567`
- `cps/web.py:1252`

Each retries 3× at `time.sleep(0.1)`, so the worst case is ~0.3s of frozen hub rather than 120s — real, but a different order of magnitude, which is why it was left out of #1385 rather than folded in.

The fix is the same one-liner: `cps.services.parallel.cooperative_sleep`. What this needs before it ships is its own red/green — the harness in `tests/unit/test_metadata_lock_gevent_responsiveness.py` measures worst heartbeat gap while a greenlet waits and transfers directly, but 0.3s sits close enough to the existing 0.3s tolerance that the threshold needs re-picking to stay decisive rather than flaky.

Worth also sweeping for the general case at the same time: the guard added in #1385 is scoped to `calibre_db_lock.py`, so nothing stops a new `time.sleep` appearing on another request path. A broader AST guard over request-path modules would close the class instead of the instances, but it needs an allowlist for the legitimate ones (`services/worker.py:124` is a real OS thread; `db.py:1285` is startup, before the hub serves anything).
title: Two more request-path time.sleep retries can freeze the gevent hub (web.py)
